definition: Building one composite reference clip out of the BEST parts of multiple separate takes — including takes from different performers reading the same line — cut together in a video editor and matched by audio waveform, rather than using any single take as-is: 'I'm kind of liking that those two are cutting together... the energy has improved because [I'm] using the energy of the second one, but the acting of the first one.'
purpose: Get a single reference clip better than any one continuous take by combining each take's own strongest moment (a better opening energy from one take, a better emotional beat from another), accepting that no single performance is likely to be the best choice all the way through.
visible_effect: The final reference clip shows visibly different energy/quality in different sections, corresponding to the specific take each section was cut from, joined at chosen cut points (matched via audio waveform) rather than being one continuous unedited performance.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: not applicable — a reference-production technique, not a viewer-facing effect on the eventual animation directly (though a stronger composite reference should produce a stronger eventual animation).
use_cases: any reference shoot where multiple takes were recorded and no single take is the best choice throughout its whole length
combining reference from two different sources (even two different performers) when each contributes something the other lacks (one performer's energy, another's specific acting choice)
non_use_cases: a reference session where one take is clearly best throughout, where splicing would add editing effort for no benefit
interactions: not applicable — the only entry in this corpus specifically about REFERENCE PRODUCTION/EDITING technique rather than animation authoring itself.
cadence_representation: Not applicable to Cadence directly: this is a pre-production video-editing technique (performed in DaVinci Resolve, outside any animation tool) that happens BEFORE a reference profile would ever be built via `ai/reference.js` — Cadence has no video-editing capability and this session found no reason it should. Worth recording anyway because of what it implies for the resulting reference's PROVENANCE: a reference profile built from a spliced, multi-take, possibly multi-performer composite is a different kind of source than a single continuous take, and if `ai/library.js`'s captured-entry provenance fields (per the existing 'a captured library entry must declare estimated: true and carry its source video URL' rule, CLAUDE.md) were ever extended to non-Roblox-capture reference sources, this composite-splice case is a concrete example of provenance that is not simply 'one URL, one timestamp range'.
control_surface: None in Cadence — the editing happens entirely outside the tool, before any reference profile is built.
detection_and_measurement_methods: not applicable — a pre-production technique, not something Cadence measures.
failure_modes: not applicable to Cadence directly, though for the source technique itself: cutting between takes at a point where the underlying motion does not actually line up (the presenter's own account of a cut 'not hooking up very well' and needing to try several different cut points before one worked)
roblox_considerations: None — entirely a pre-production reference technique.
examples: the presenter's own words, verbatim, splicing between two different performers' takes: 'I'm kind of like in that way that those two are cutting together... the energy has improved because [I'm] using the energy of the second one, but the acting of the first one' (transcript 18:15-18:24), and the general method stated earlier in the same editing pass: 'it's also helpful to leave the audio running out of your computer[,] so then you can literally just match the wave form' (transcript 19:34-19:36)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/TaiJauNiKH4 @ 19:34-19:36 and 18:15-18:24 — owenferny demonstrates splicing multiple takes (including two different performers) together via audio-waveform-matched cuts in DaVinci Resolve, transcript-only per this video's detail setting; experimental until validated
